fx.fx_commentary: The Canadian dollar settled at 0.7161 against the US dollar, easing 0.14% on the week and 2.63% year-over-year — the move came as the US funds ceiling held at 3.75% versus the Bank of Canada overnight rate at 2.25%, holding the Fed-BoC differential near 125 basis points following the June 10 BoC decision to hold for a second consecutive meeting.121 Commodity flows added pressure as WTI fell 11.74% to US$80.58/bbl on the week.32 The euro rose to 1.1600 (+0.87% on the week, flat year-over-year) after the European Central Bank lifted its deposit facility rate 25 basis points to 2.25% effective June 17 — the first ECB hike in three years, narrowing the ECB-BoC differential to zero.26 Sterling traded at 1.3450 (+0.86% on the week, -1.31% year-over-year) after the Bank of England's 8-1 vote on April 30 to hold Bank Rate at 3.75%, ahead of the June 18 MPC meeting.28 The dollar sat at 159.9550 against the yen (-0.06%) and 6.7600 against the offshore yuan (-0.08% on the week, -6.02% year-over-year).32 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties the CAD/USD level to 346 active Canadian manufacturing projects ($70.0B aggregate) priced against US-denominated capital equipment.32 If the loonie holds near current levels through the third quarter, those 346 manufacturing projects would face landed-cost pressure on imported machinery inputs flagged in 2026 capex intentions of $401,203M.11

yieldCurve.yield_commentary: The Government of Canada yield curve held a normal slope with the 2s10s spread at +64 basis points — the 10Y benchmark sat at 3.40% versus the 2Y at 2.76%, following the Bank of Canada's June 10 decision to hold the overnight rate at 2.25% for the second consecutive meeting alongside the June Monetary Policy Report.1 Year-over-year the 2Y has risen 5 basis points from 2.71%, the 5Y 8 basis points from 2.96% to 3.04%, the 10Y 3 basis points from 3.37%, and the long bond 17 basis points from 3.65% to 3.82%, a steeper back-end term-premium pickup than at the front.32 The 5Y benchmark at 3.04% remains the residential mortgage-renewal anchor cited in the June MPR.2 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties the curve to 1,862 active rate-sensitive Canadian projects ($284.3B aggregate) financed against the GoC term structure, with 272 residential projects ($41.6B) most directly exposed to 5Y pricing for mortgage refinancing.32 If the 5Y benchmark holds above three percent through the third quarter, the 272 residential projects would face renewal pricing 8 basis points wider than the year-ago benchmark, while the broader rate-sensitive book priced off the 10Y would carry roughly 3 basis points of additional cost versus the same window in 2025.32
